topProblems: The endcard is narrator-only and generic — 'genuine, or just smooth?' is engagement-bait, not a punchline. The word-count gag deserves a joke button, and Brock/Matteo/Lucas all exit unresolved so the episode stops rather than lands.
Lucas's poolside 'cold war' is declared and then abandoned. It's the only escalation beat that causes nothing downstream — he isn't even in the terrace crowd shot when the six drops.
Scene 5 (no-music dance) doesn't causally follow Scene 4 (Brock's crack). Two beats sit in parallel instead of one triggering the next, softening the run-up to the record six.

Syntax uniformity flattens voice: nearly every line is a clipped 3-6 word fragment ('You made noise. I made brunch.' / 'That's a threat.' / 'He dances? That's my whole thing.'). Only Brock's bellow breaks rhythm. Poppy — the villa's designated commentator — gets two lines total.
Narrator does too much of the comic lifting in scenes 3 and 5 (four of seven lines), so the cast becomes reaction props in the middle third.
concreteFixes: Scene 7 endcard: replace the third narrator line with a character button that pays the word count — Alejandro finally speaks and it's something devastatingly mundane ('Where is the blender?'), narrator: 'Three words left.' Keep 'Comment. Loudly.' as the fourth beat only if Brock is heard yelling it off-screen.

Scene 3: give Lucas a consequence, not just a reaction. Have him challenge Alejandro on the spot ('Dance-off. Sunset.') so the cold war becomes a scheduled event the audience waits for, then plant Sienna one line converting it into a dare to keep the thread live.

Chain scene 4 to scene 5: end Brock's confessional with him saying he'll 'go louder,' then open scene 5 with Brock's music cutting out (he blew the speaker) — which is WHY Alejandro dances with no music. Now the dance is caused, and Brock caused it.

Scene 6: bring Lucas onto the terrace and give him the fourth reaction after Brock and Matteo ('I've been dancing for eleven years. What did I get?' — Élodie: 'Five.') so the record six pays off three rivals instead of two.

Scene 2: break the fragment rhythm. Let Matteo run one operatic long sentence (12+ words, escalating clause on clause about the brunch) so his voice is structurally different from Poppy's and Élodie's clipped lines.

Scene 1: give Poppy a second line after Brock's 'Full send' so she gets a setup-and-topper instead of a single quip — e.g. she names the smoothie as evidence ('Pink. Chunky. Unsolicited.') before 'That's a threat,' letting the joke breathe.

aiDefects: All four characters are hard-cropped at the frame bottom and read as flat cutouts pasted over the background rather than standing in the scene (no contact shadows, no occlusion by the fire-pit bench)
Italian character's hands on the pasta bowl are soft/fused — finger separation is mushy and the left thumb reads melted
US character's bottle-holding hand is partially cut by the frame edge and the grip does not wrap the bottle convincingly
Spanish character's right arm disappears behind his hip with no resolved hand
Scale/perspective mismatch: heads are far too large relative to the fire pit and seating ring directly behind them
Bonfire flame plane sits oddly between characters with no light spill onto their faces or bodies
images.notes: Glossy candy-bright grading, purple-to-orange sunset and lantern strings are on-model for the house style, and the wardrobe reads instantly (stars-and-stripes tank/cap, Italian tricolore apron, French beret + Breton stripes + tricolore neckerchief, Spanish red shirt with flag patch). However the foreground cast is composited rather than integrated: no contact shadows, no firelight rim, mismatched scale, and warped hands on the pasta bowl. A viewer would clock this as an AI/cutout composite.

images.notes: Best-integrated of the three: warm golden-hour grade, bougainvillea and sailboat backdrop match the house look, and character proportions (big heads, glossy skin, stylized eyes) are consistent with frames 0 and 1. Flag wardrobe is immediately legible — US stars-and-stripes tank, Union Jack crop set with matching mug, Italian tricolore apron, French beret with cockade plus Breton stripes. Remaining issues are soft hands on the mug/bottle and the usual cutout stacking, which is imperfect but shippable.

visuals.overallNotes: The three stills share a coherent, glossy candy-bright 3D look — same saturated grade, same plush cartoon proportions, same character designs and costumes frame to frame — and every nationality reads at a glance from flag-colored wardrobe, which is the strongest part of the set. The systemic problem is compositing: in all three frames the cast is a hard-cropped foreground strip with no contact shadows, no environmental light spill (bonfire, candle, pool caustics all ignored) and inconsistent scale against their backgrounds, which is exactly the tell that makes a viewer say 'this is AI.' Secondary recurring defect is hands: every prop-holding hand (bottle, pasta bowl, mug) has fused or soft fingers. Frame 1 adds a genuinely broken prop — the floating pool buffet with melted drinks and an impossible tray angle. Recommended fixes before ship: re-render or paint in contact shadows and rim light from each scene's key source, nudge character scale down ~10-15% so head sizes agree with background architecture, clean up all three prop grips, and rebuild or blur the pool float tray.
